the_limiting_factor_measured: verification coverage. 3 of 13 ordinary goals were checkable; the other 10 were refused because success could not be established without a reference answer.

web_grounding.property_based_testing_vs_alternatives: 82.7% correctness vs 58.3% baseline, and vs 77.3% for the agent judging its own output; fuzzing 79.1%; TDD 61.8%
web_grounding.the_insight_used: ask whether the output satisfies properties any correct output must satisfy, instead of asking whether it equals a reference
web_grounding.also_used: Oracle independence: a verdict is worth only as much as the distance between the evidence source and the system that produced the work
web_grounding.warning_heeded: WebVoyager's judge produces false positives at 45%+; a verifier that only says YES is a rubber stamp

what_was_built.idea: for a recognised verb the CORRECT OUTPUT IS DEFINED BY THE INPUT, so no reference answer is needed
what_was_built.refused_verbs: summarise, translate, rewrite, paraphrase, explain, describe, improve, fix, clean, format, beautify, analysis, review, refactor

what_this_does_not_claim: that computer use is solved. Nine relations on .txt/.md moved from impossible to checkable; the rest of the machine is unchanged.
that the MiniWob number moved. It is a GUI path and is untouched at 56.3%.
that the three TransferTests pass. They encode a contradiction (see R148) and are untouched.
the_answer_to_the_user: instant learning is real and permanent (measured: recall in 0.0 s across processes). It does not generalise to all computer use for one reason only -- the machine must be able to tell that the one time it ran, it worked. Every goal given a verifier becomes learnable forever. That is the whole bottleneck, and this round added nine verifiers.
